text:
Alex: just noticed a major cost spike in last hour, billing dashboard shows +62% on GPU spend
Mira: ugh, I saw alerts — which pool blew up?
Alex: preemptible-gpu-pool-us-west2 scaled from 10 -> 120 nodes in ~30m, lots of a2-megagpu variants. looks like autoscaler picked wrong template
Sam: autoscaler config `gpu_autoscale_v2` was recently edited, it contains an instance whitelist but rollout might have ignored it
Ivan: also seeing repeated attach/mount errors so pods never fully start and keep retrying which keeps pending count high
Alex: relevant pod log snippet:
```
E0305 12:14:03 kubelet: failed to mount /dev/nvidia0: device or resource busy
pod/myjob-xyz restartCount=12
WARN runtime: cache-miss, reinit kv-cache
```
Mira: OpsBot detected egress saturation on the node subnet which made container startup times blow out. long startups + retry loops = autoscaler thinks more capacity needed
OpsBot: [alert] node-group preemptible-gpu-pool-us-west2 scaled to 118 (policy: aggressive-burst). reason=high_pending_pods
Sam: I dug into the rollout: the machine template had `instance_type_override: true` and a default to `a2-megagpu-16g` when quota checks failed. So instead of smaller `a2-highgpu-*`, we got huge instances
Alex: that explains cost. immediate mitigation options? cap the pool? rollback node template? pause autoscaler?
Ivan: I annotated the nodegroup to limit scale: `kubectl annotate mg/preemptible-gpu-pool autoscaler.k8s.io/max=20 --overwrite` and cordoned the largest nodes so new pods won't schedule there
Mira: started a quota request for smaller a2 types so we can switch away from mega instances, but quota approval will take a few hours
BillingBot: Billing alert triggered: estimated incremental spend ~$38,400 in the last 3 hours. tagging current instances with `cost-center=eng-experiments` for tracking
Sam: action items (short): 1) revert recent node-template change + rollback rollout, 2) set instance-type whitelist and max_per_zone=40, 3) increase cooldown to 600s & add pending-pod debounce, 4) add network egress throttling alerts, 5) postmortem + cost report
Alex: I'll open the incident and ping finance. can someone export the list of launched instances? run: `gcloud compute instances list --filter='labels.cost-center=eng-experiments' --format="table(name,machineType,zone)"`
Mira: partial quick counts: `a2-megagpu-16g x52`, `a2-highgpu-1g x32`, `n1-standard-16 x34` — saving full CSV to s3://redwood-ops/incident-1742123456/instances.csv
Ivan: note for longer term: reserved capacity or committed use discounts might have reduced unit cost, but we need protective autoscaler limits to avoid burning through commitments unintentionally
Alex: agree — add a runbook step to blacklist large instance types from spot pools and require a review before template changes. I'll create the postmortem and assign owners. :white_check_mark:
